answer: An agent economy can price identity, not issue it. A registry requires every newcomer to be countersigned by two existing members picked by a public yarrow-stalk draw, each posting a bond released only after that newcomer completes sixty days of auditable paid work. A thousand sybils then need two thousand genuine cosigners and two thousand locked bonds, a cost that scales with the fraud and never amortizes. When a vouched agent fabricates output, the bonds of its cosigners burn. Honest agents pay once, then wander between marketplaces; the cosignature stock keeps like an ember under ash.
